question: Should publisher follow notifications and capped in-mutation fanout become the supported ClawHub product/API surface after the follow stack lands?
rationale: This PR adds new private user notification state and publication-delivery semantics, and automation cannot decide the long-term product boundary or accept the capped fanout tradeoff for maintainers.

options.title: Require proof and gate fix first
options.body: Fix the package-release visibility gate, require real runtime proof, and decide the product/API boundary after the base stack is reviewable.

options.title: Pause notification delivery
options.body: Keep or close this notification slice until the base follow graph and controls PRs are accepted and proven.

options.title: Sponsor the feature as-is conceptually
options.body: Maintainers may accept the capped fanout direction, but still need the code defect fixed and real behavior proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Require proof and gate fix first
recommendation.body: Fix the package-release visibility gate, require real runtime proof, and decide the product/API boundary after the base stack is reviewable.

likelyOwner.reason: The central decision crosses the existing package/skill publish path and schema/API surfaces tied to this history.
